articles.excerpt: Most name-and-number personalizers drop flat text on top of a photo. Shoppers can tell. The jersey store I build for wanted the opposite: a preview that looks like the real printed shirt, in each club…
articles.body: Most name-and-number personalizers drop flat text on top of a photo. Shoppers can tell. The jersey store I build for wanted the opposite: a preview that looks like the real printed shirt, in each club's own lettering. It now runs on 285 live jerseys across 83 kit styles , from one canvas script inside the theme. No app, no per-order fee. How it works The back photo of the shirt goes onto a canvas. The name and number are drawn in the club's font, warped through a mesh for perspective and curve ( 48 columns minimum, about 3 px wide on larger prints), then shaded with the photo itself. The finished image is attached to the order, so production prints what the shopper saw. Three things broke on the way. 1. The font that rendered at 10px The name appeared, but tiny.

articles.body: Short answer Project Zomboid (The Indie Stone, Early Access November 8, 2013) runs on Java with LWJGL — the Lightweight Java Game Library — plus Lua for gameplay and mods . The infobox lists Engine: LWJGL , and the community wiki is blunter: Coded in Java and Lua . That looks outdated in 2026. It is the point. Most survival hits rent Unity or Unreal for lighting and marketing. Zomboid stayed on a thin Java wrapper over C libraries for 13+ years, from a 2011 pre-alpha to Stable Build 42.22.2 . Steam still describes it as long Early Access with monthly Unstable betas, full Lua modding access, and many 1,000+ hour players . My take, stated as opinion not fact: Zomboid did not survive despite Java.

articles.title: Why Is My Crypto Withdrawal Still Pending?
articles.excerpt: Why is my crypto withdrawal still pending? Usually it is waiting for the platform to process it, for the blockchain to confirm it, or for a review or fee condition to clear. You can narrow down the ca…
articles.body: Why is my crypto withdrawal still pending? Usually it is waiting for the platform to process it, for the blockchain to confirm it, or for a review or fee condition to clear. You can narrow down the cause in a few checks: the platform status, the transaction ID on the block explorer, and the network and address you used. Why is my crypto withdrawal still pending? "Pending" means the transfer has been requested but is not final yet. The delay usually comes from one of these places: Platform processing: Exchanges and wallet apps often batch withdrawals or run their own checks before they broadcast the transaction to the network. Blockchain confirmations: The transaction is on the network but has not reached the number of confirmations the platform requires before it counts as complete.

articles.title: Android 14 foreground services: the specialUse migration that saved our VPN
articles.excerpt: TL;DR — On Android 14 a regular app cannot start a foreground service with systemExempted: startForeground() throws SecurityException, the service silently dies, and the user just sees "VPN is not wor…
articles.body: TL;DR — On Android 14 a regular app cannot start a foreground service with systemExempted : startForeground() throws SecurityException , the service silently dies, and the user just sees "VPN is not working". For a VPN client that isn't a system app, the working path is specialUse + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE + a vpn subtype in the manifest. Context I maintain an Android VPN client built on VpnService . Since API 26 it runs as a foreground service: persistent notification, startForegroundService() , startForeground() inside the service. That worked fine on Android 8–13. Android 14 (API 34) tightened the rules: every foreground service must declare a type, and the type must be allowed for the app.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 15, 1988: The 300-foot Green Bank Telescope collapses suddenly, leaving a huge pile of wreckage in West Virginia
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. It happened at 9:46 p.m. on a clear night with no strong winds. When the observatory staff showed up to work the next morning, they were greeted by a huge pile of wreckage. The telescope collapsed under its own weight after a key structural element called a "gusset plate" failed. This was one of four connecting plates that held the telescope's large, metal beams together. Investigators found that these gusset plates were not built to last the 26 years that this telescope had been in use. Three years later, construction began on a new telescope. The Green Bank Telescope was even bigger and more sensitive, and it began science operations in 2001.

articles.body: For the past two years, stargazers have waited with bated breath for a "new" light to appear in the night sky, born of one of the most cataclysmic events known to occur in the cosmos — a nova explosion. But what is the "Blaze Star" T. Coronae Borealis, and why is it so difficult to predict when its overdue brightening will occur? We turned to the experts to find out. What is T. Coronae Borealis? T. Coronae Borealis — or T CrB for short — isn't a single star, but rather a binary system containing a dense white dwarf star and a bloated red giant. Over a period of around 80 years, the white dwarf's gravity strips material from the red giant until it hits a critical threshold.

articles.title: How escaping gases ripped apart a comet and caused it to become thousands of times brighter
articles.excerpt: This summer, comet 220P/McNaught burst into life out of nowhere to become one of the year’s highlights for amateur astronomers.
articles.body: A comet dazzled this summer as the sun’s heat caused ice beneath its surface to turn to gas and rip out through its surface, spewing hundreds of billions of pounds' worth of dust into space and causing the comet to brighten by thousands of times. Comet 220P/McNaught was discovered by the prolific Australian comet discoverer Robert McNaught in 2004. It is a periodic comet, the 220th discovered, meaning that it comes back again and again on a regular basis – in 220P’s case, once every five-and-a-half years when it gets about as close to the sun as Mars . Other than that, 220P is fairly nondescript, usually languishing at a feeble brightness fainter than magnitude +15, out of reach of most amateur telescopes. There has been little else to say about the comet, until this year.
articles.author: Keith Cooper

articles.title: What's next for SpaceX's Starship after epic Flight 15 chopsticks catch?
articles.excerpt: SpaceX just made spaceflight history, catching the upper stage of its Starship megarocket when it returned to Earth. But Starship still has some pretty big boxes left to check.
articles.body: Starship may have just made history, but it still has some work to do to get fully up and running. The megarocket launched on its 15th test flight on Friday (Nov. 13), aiming to pull off a dramatic and unprecedented twofer. SpaceX wanted to bring both Starship elements — its Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — back to the launch pad at its Starbase site in Texas to be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. It didn't happen with Super Heavy; the booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday evening after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship came home successfully , nestling into the tower's arms in a soft and unprecedented embrace on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after lifting off. Long-distance view of Ship's historic landing on Nov. 14, 2026.
